claims.text: A StorageClass contains the field provisioner (plus parameters, reclaimPolicy), used when a PersistentVolume of that class is dynamically provisioned to satisfy a PVC; a claim requests a class by naming it in storageClassName.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Storage Classes > StorageClass objects; refs/kubernetes-website/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes.md

claims.text: Dynamic volume provisioning creates storage volumes on demand, so cluster administrators do not have to create them (and their PersistentVolume objects) manually ahead of time.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Dynamic Volume Provisioning (intro); refs/kubernetes-website/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/dynamic-provisioning.md

claims.text: When a PVC does not specify storageClassName, the default StorageClass is used; a cluster can have no default StorageClass at all.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Default StorageClass; Persistent Volumes > Class

claims.text: In the kind cluster donhang (kind v0.33), kubectl get storageclass shows one class, standard (default), provisioner rancher.io/local-path, VOLUMEBINDINGMODE WaitForFirstConsumer (storage-class.txt lines 1-3).

WaitForFirstConsumer delays binding and provisioning of a PersistentVolume until a Pod using the PVC is created; the PV is provisioned conforming to the Pod's scheduling constraints. Before that the claim is Pending with no PV (storage-class.txt line 7).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Volume binding mode; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/storage-class.txt lines 5-10

claims.text: With standard, the provisioner creates the volume as a folder under /var/local-path-provisioner/ on the node kube-scheduler chose for writer, and the PV's nodeAffinity names that node (storage-class.txt lines 12-16; storage-class.sh lines 28-29).
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/storage-class.txt lines 12-16; scripts/k8s/storage-class.sh lines 28-35 at stage-3; local-path-provisioner README (node affinity by hostname)

claims.text: A PV can specify node affinity limiting which nodes it can be accessed from; Pods that use the PV are only scheduled to nodes selected by that node affinity.
kubectl cordon marks a node unschedulable: the scheduler places no new Pods on it, Pods already on it are not affected; kubectl uncordon makes it schedulable again.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes > Manual Node administration (kubectl cordon)

claims.text: When the scheduler cannot place a Pod it records one FailedScheduling event whose message lists why each node was ruled out. Cordoned case: writer stays Pending; 1 node failed PV node affinity, 1 untolerated taints, 1 unschedulable; after uncordon it runs (storage-class.txt 18-32).

Mapping of the three FailedScheduling reasons: the other worker fails node affinity, writer's node is unschedulable, the control-plane node is excluded (by its taint; the lesson only says 'for a reason outside this lesson').
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: well-known taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane; deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml (1 control-plane, 2 workers)

claims.text: kind runs each node as a Docker container; deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml at stage-3 declares one control-plane and two workers and sets no extraMounts, so no host folder is mapped into the nodes.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml lines 1-14 at stage-3; kind.sigs.k8s.io quick-start and configuration (extraMounts)

claims.text: The local-path folder is inside one kind node; no other node or host folder holds it, so losing that node loses the folder for the cluster, and kind delete cluster (scripts/k8s/cluster-down.sh) removes every node container, the folder with it.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: configuration (extraMounts, persisting data), quick-start (Deleting a Cluster); cluster-down.sh lines 2,7 at stage-3; kind docker provider DeleteNodes

claims.text: Copies of a volume on other nodes require a provisioner designed for it; local-path keeps each volume on the one node where it was provisioned.
claims.source_hint: local-path-provisioner README (node-local storage, volume only accessible on the node where provisioned)

claims.text: volumeBindingMode Immediate: binding and dynamic provisioning occur once the PVC is created, without knowledge of Pod scheduling.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Volume binding mode

claims.text: deploy/k8s/lessons/data-pvc.yaml at stage-3: PVC data, namespace storage-lessons, ReadWriteOnce, 100Mi, no storageClassName; comment lines 4-5 say the default StorageClass provides it (standard in kind).

storage-class.sh at stage-3: L6 show echoes $ cmd, runs it; 21-22 sleep 5, count PVs; 30-32 Pod node, PV, PV node; 34 class, policy, hostPath or local path; 35 compare; 41-44 cordon, delete, reapply; 48-49 last FailedScheduling event, sed cuts 0/N; 53-56 uncordon.
Which StorageClass is default depends on what was marked default in that cluster (by its administrators, or set by e.g. a cloud provider); different provisioners and binding modes behave differently.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Default StorageClass; Dynamic Volume Provisioning > Defaulting Behavior

claims.text: kube-scheduler records the chosen node on the PVC (annotation volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node) via the API server; the provisioner runs in the cluster and reads claims through the API server, so only then does it create the folder on that node and the PV.
claims.source_hint: refs/.../reference/labels-annotations-taints/_index.md, volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node; local-path-provisioner README (runs in the cluster, watches PVCs)

claims.text: The default columns of kubectl get pv are NAME, CAPACITY, ACCESS MODES, RECLAIM POLICY, STATUS, CLAIM, STORAGECLASS, REASON, AGE: none names the provisioner (that is in annotation pv.kubernetes.io/provisioned-by).
